command.description: Every command that writes a result artifact, in alphabetical order. `export` and `server-db` were absent while emitting artifacts that named them, so those artifacts violated this schema; tests/unit/test_result_schema_matches_commands.py binds the enum to what the code actually emits and to what the CLI actually defines.

protocol.description: Every member of apiverity.core.model.Protocol, in declaration order. Adding a protocol to that enum without adding it here makes `validate --json` emit an artifact that violates this schema; tests/unit/test_result_schema_matches_protocols.py binds the two so the omission fails the build instead of shipping.

target.description: Base URL contacted, or null when nothing was contacted.

seed.description: Generation seed, or null when the command is not seeded.

operation_key.description: Operation the finding belongs to, or null for contract-level findings.

tool.description: MCP tool a finding belongs to, when the protocol has one.

occurrences.description: Entries in which this finding occurred (corpus drift).

observations.description: Entries that could have produced it (corpus drift).

frequency.description: occurrences / observations, rounded to four places.

first_seen.description: Earliest timestamp the corpus recorded for this finding.

examples.description: A capped set of example request URLs, not a second copy of the corpus.

change_id.description: The CHG-* id behind a schema-drift or breaking finding. Null on findings that did not come from a diff.

source_rule_id.description: The BRK-* rule that classified it, so a drift finding traces back to the shared catalogue.

trace_id.description: Trace this finding's run belongs to, when the run was traced. Absent otherwise -- never an id that resolves to nothing.

span_id.description: The span of the call this finding was read out of, so it can be opened in a tracing backend.

hint.description: What to do about it, when the rule knows.

status.description: HTTP status a probe observed, on findings that came from one.

source.description: Where a candidate route came from: a previous contract, or a recorded corpus.

state.description: Set when a drift run was given a baseline: `known` was already there, `new` is what this run added. Only new findings fail the run; known ones stay in the artifact.

items.description: One finding, in the shape every command emits. `apiverity drift` has four detection modes and each returned a differently-shaped report nested under `report`, outside this contract entirely; every mode now also writes this array. The optional fields below are contributed by the modes that can establish them -- absent means the mode cannot, which is not the same as zero.

operation_count.description: Number of operations in the contract (validate, self-test).
